title: FizzBuzz
directAnswer: For each i: if divisible by 3 AND 5 → FizzBuzz, else by 3 → Fizz, else by 5 → Buzz, else the number. Check the both-case first.

remember.takeaway: When conditions overlap, test the most specific one first.
antiSignals: Checking general cases before the most specific one

problemStatement: Given `n`, return a list of strings for 1..n where multiples of 3 are `"Fizz"`, multiples of 5 are `"Buzz"`, multiples of both are `"FizzBuzz"`, and others are the number itself.
understanding: Check divisibility by 15 (both) first, then 3, then 5, else the number.

approaches.name: Ordered divisibility checks
approaches.whenToMention: This is the standard, expected solution — lead with it.
approaches.explanation:
The canonical screening problem. For each i in 1..n: multiples of both 3 and 5 → "FizzBuzz", multiples of 3 → "Fizz", multiples of 5 → "Buzz", otherwise the number. The entire test is **branch ordering**.

**Why test divisible-by-15 first.** Every multiple of 15 is also a multiple of 3 and of 5. If you check `% 3` before `% 15`, then 15, 30, 45… match the Fizz branch and never produce "FizzBuzz". So the most specific condition (both) must come first. This is the trap the problem is famous for.

**The append variant (no 15 check).** Build the word incrementally: append "Fizz" if divisible by 3, append "Buzz" if divisible by 5; if the word is still empty, use the number. This avoids the explicit 15 test and extends naturally to more divisors (e.g. add 7 → "Bazz").

**Output type.** Return strings, not ints — the number case must be stringified too.
hints: Which numbers satisfy more than one rule, and why does order matter?
Alternative: append 'Fizz'/'Buzz' and fall back to the number if empty.
approaches.insight: A clean variant builds the word by appending 'Fizz' then 'Buzz' and falls back to the number if empty — no 15 check needed.
approaches.complexityReasoning: one constant set of divisibility checks per number across n numbers.

java.explanation: Check the combined case first, before 3 and 5.

pitfalls: Checking %3 or %5 before %15, so 15 never prints FizzBuzz.

commonMistakes: Checking %3 or %5 before %15, so 15 never prints FizzBuzz.
patternNote: A core fresher pattern: Ordered branch (most-specific first). Master it on small inputs and it transfers to harder problems.

commonMistakesDetailed.title: Wrong branch order
commonMistakesDetailed.why: Testing %3 before %15 makes every multiple of 15 print 'Fizz', never 'FizzBuzz'.
commonMistakesDetailed.bad:
if i%3==0: 'Fizz'
elif i%5==0: 'Buzz'
elif i%15==0: 'FizzBuzz'  # unreachable
commonMistakesDetailed.good:
if i%15==0: 'FizzBuzz'
elif i%3==0: 'Fizz'
elif i%5==0: 'Buzz'
